column2: Prepare breadboard 2 (the second 400-hole breadboard; the first one is used by the body). The breadboard has no power of its own: its power comes from the S3 expansion board. One wire from the 3V3 pin in the 3V3 block of the S3 expansion board → the upper red line, one wire from a G pin of the S3 expansion board → the upper blue line. The screen, MAX98357A, and INMP441 get their power from these two lines (the S3 itself runs from USB in bench mode). The MAX98357A will be plugged into columns 12-18 and the INMP441 into columns 26-28 of this breadboard; columns 21-23 are kept free for the finished robot's STOP button.
F-M and M-M jumper wires
The connections run through breadboard columns: the module pin is in row e, its wire is in row a of the same column.

Plug the MAX98357A into breadboard 2 with its seven pins in row e, columns 12 to 18: e12 LRC, e13 BCLK, e14 DIN, e15 GAIN, e16 SD, e17 GND, e18 Vin. The module body spans over the middle gap toward rows f-j. Push until the pins are fully in.
M-M wires from a hole in the same column: a17 (GND) → blue line, a18 (Vin) → red line (3.3 V, for bench use).
F-M wires from the S pins of the expansion board: IO4 → a13 (BCLK), IO5 → a12 (LRC), IO7 → a14 (DIN). Columns 15 and 16 (GAIN and SD) stay empty.

Final floor 3 (front on the left of the photo): S3 at the rear, breadboard 2 in the middle, the TFT on the robot's right edge (top of the photo) with the SD slot on top, the speaker on the left edge (bottom of the photo). On the finished robot, the MAX98357A and INMP441 are plugged into breadboard 2 (see the layout drawing); the head in the photo is still lying down.

Floor 3 (third plate): the S3 board at the rear end with its USB-C port facing sideways, breadboard 2 in front of it with the MAX98357A, STOP button, and INMP441 plugged into it (the microphone at the end far from the speaker), the TFT standing on the right edge with the SD card slot on top, the pan-tilt head with the ESP32-CAM at the front end, and the box speaker standing on the left edge.

Fill the third plate while it is still on the table: the S3 board (together with breadboard 2 and the wiring from Part 3) on 10 mm nylon spacers, the TFT standing on the right edge, screen facing outward and the SD card slot on top so the card is easy to pull out (screen orientation 6), held upright with a small bracket or tied with cable ties to a spacer, breadboard 2 tied with cable ties with its column 1 end on the speaker side (the MAX98357A and INMP441 stay plugged in as in Part 3, so the microphone in columns 26-28 ends up far from the speaker), the pan-tilt head bolted at the front with the pan axis in the middle of the plate width, and the speaker standing on the left edge, tied with two cable ties through the holes of the left middle wing.

STOP button on breadboard 2, columns 21-23: plug the tactile button across the middle gap with its legs in e21, e23, f21, f23. Push until the legs are fully in. Attach two 25 cm (no. 28) jumper wires to the columns of two diagonal legs: a21 and j23. Do not connect columns 21 and 23 to the red or blue rails of breadboard 2, or to S3 pins: this button belongs to the body on floor 2.
Move the end of the wire in a18 (MAX98357A Vin) from the 3.3 V red rail to the 5V pin of the S3 board, so the speaker is louder and does not load the 3.3 V. The INMP441 stays on the 3.3 V rail.

Battery switch OFF. Cut green 22 AWG 10 cm (no. 17) and black 10 cm (no. 18). Solder one end of each to a 3 cm female jumper piece, heat shrink. Green: WAGO 6V → VM. Black: WAGO −6 → the third GND on the right side, right below VCC (order VM, VCC, GND). All three GND pins of the TB6612 are connected inside the board, so another GND still works.

Level-1 connections: motor wires to AO1/AO2 and BO1/BO2 of the TB6612, green-black from WAGO 6V/−6 to VM and GND of the TB6612 (the third GND on the right side, right below VCC) and the 470 µF capacitor on WAGO 6V/−6 (Part 2), the WAGO +/− wires to the IN of both LM2596 (Part 1).

Cut red 26 AWG wire 18 cm (no. 24) and put 2 mm of blue heat shrink on both ends to mark it as the battery sense wire: clamp one end in the IN+ terminal of LM2596 #1 together with its red wire (the battery plus rail after the switch), the other end to a20. Stranded 26 AWG wire bends easily and sits loose in a breadboard, so solder the breadboard end to a 3 cm male jumper piece (left over from an M-M wire), heat shrink, then plug it into a20. Not from P+ before the fuse.
4 female jumper pieces 3 cm + heat shrink

Upper ends of the 5 V + GND wires to the 30P board (21 cm (no. 21)) and the S3 board (23 cm (no. 22)): the 5V and GND pins in the power block of both boards are male pins, so solder each end (red and black, 4 ends) to a 3 cm female jumper piece like the TB6612 wires in Part 2, then cover with heat shrink. Pull gently to check the solder joint. These red ends are the ones you unplug and plug when switching between bench mode and running mode.
rear HC-SR04 → breadboard 1 (join F-F + M-M)

Signal wires going up: 9 F-F wires from the TB6612 (to the 30P board, 20 cm is enough), 4 F-F wires from the MPU6050 (to the I2C header of the 30P board, 18 cm (no. 31)), 4 wires from the rear HC-SR04 (to breadboard 1, 28 cm (no. 30): longer than a 20 cm jumper, so join each wire, F-F at the sensor then M-M to the breadboard, with the joint wrapped in tape; or use 30 cm jumpers).
